course.title: XML — From Beginner to Advanced
course.description: A visual-first XML curriculum covering syntax, document design, namespaces, DTD/XSD validation, XPath, XSLT, optional XQuery and advanced specifications, parsing, serialization, services, security, testing, performance, real-world formats, and professional maintenance.
course.version_scope: Standards references checked 2026-10-12. Core XML syntax follows XML 1.0; XPath/XSLT/XQuery/XSD lessons distinguish specification versions from actual processor support. Recheck current errata, implementations, security guidance and dependency versions before publication.
prerequisites: No programming experience required. Basic familiarity with files, folders, and a text editor is helpful. Specialist processors are needed for DTD/XSD validation, XPath, XSLT, and XQuery examples.
learning_outcomes: Create and inspect well-formed XML documents with correct characters, declarations, and namespaces.
Design document structures and validate constraints using DTD and XML Schema (XSD).
Query and transform XML with XPath, XSLT, and optional XQuery in version-compatible processors.
Process and serialize XML using browser/backend APIs and select tree versus streaming approaches.
Apply secure parsing, testing, interoperability, performance, schema governance and migration practices.

source_pdf.source_note: The 38-page PDF was rendered and inspected as four contact sheets covering pages 1–38 and its text layer was parsed. The curriculum lists a continuous sequence of 176 lesson identifiers. Page 11 places lessons 57–79 under the DTD heading, but pages 13–15 explicitly start an XSD module at lesson 66; this course separates DTD lessons 57–65 (module 8) and XSD lessons 66–79 (module 9). No lesson IDs were invented.
